Bwana Tembo Safari Camp
Bwanda Tembo Safari Camp is located in the north-western region of Uganda. It’s situated about 6km from Tangi gate entering Murchison Falls National Park. Bwana Tembo is an exclusive safari camp located just near to Murchison Falls National Park.
The name “Bwana Tembo” means “Sir Elephant” or “Master Elephant”. Various herds of elephants visited the location during construction, leading to the camp’s naming. Until now, these majestic animals have primarily visited the premises at night and departed early in the morning.
Bwana Tembo Lodge proposes a breath-taking views of the great park. There are variety of birds frequently spotted on the camp’s premises and it’s renowned for its mouth-watering Italian cuisine that leaves tourists wanting more.
The camp offers services of best quality at reasonable prices. It’s an eco-friendly, with solar power systems working 24 hours a day. It features six self-contained cottages and four spacious elevated safari tents. The staff are friendly and often share their park experiences with guests.
Bwana Tembo Safari Camp is a very calm place thus being a perfect place to relax and enjoy the sounds of nature while overlooking the White Nile. This charming family-run safari camp is about 10 kilometers from the park’s northern gate. The camp has been offering a friendly and laid-back ambiance for travelers wishing to find the perfect getaway from the stress of everyday life ever since it opened its doors. Whether you are looking for a relaxing experience or something more adventurous, upon your arrival sit yourself to a cup of Italian espresso and organize your tour with Davide and Francesco, owners and managers of the camp, profoundly knowledgeable of the park and its surroundings.
The camp is a concoction of mid-range prices with the best quality services. The fact being that it is owned and managed by Italians, yes what could you expect, of course, Italian delicacies!! The fresh homemade Italian cuisine is prepared to the highest standards and is mouth-wateringly good. The chefs are all trained by mamma Nicoletta who is sometimes present to supervise meal preparations and give the final touches to the great three-course menu served. From time to time she will also do some cooking herself and the dishes will have that something special that only she can give.
The camp, sprawled just a kilometer from the White Nile, is comprised of both cottages and safari tents to suit the needs of a diverse clientele. All accommodation types are self-contained with flushing toilets, hand basins, and showers with hot and cold running water. Lights are set up inside and outside of the accommodations and each cottage or tent has its own veranda. The camp is entirely eco-friendly, with solar power systems ensuring that all accommodations have light throughout the day and night.
Rooms at Bwana Tembo Safari Camp
Safari camp features cottages and safari tents raised at on magnificent platforms which is good for spectacular nature views.
All accommodation rooms are self-contained decorated with en-suite facilities of the Italian stylized arrases. All rooms have access to electricity and hot water at any time during the day and night.
Every room has amenities include balcony/deck, private bathroom, fan, mosquito nets, linen, safe, hot showers, smoking rooms, and daily housekeeping.
Cottage
A simple, well-designed, and cozy room with a private bathroom containing hot water is always available for showering. All cottages contain a fan that can be operated at the guest’s discretion. A huge mosquito net encircles the beds, and in every restroom there is a large container of safe drinking water. The water supply has been thoroughly purified and is completely secure.
Safari Tent
The safari tents are custom-made 4×4 meter tents, each of the tent has a private bathroom with hot water, a sink, a flush toilet, and a light. The tents are built on a raised wooden terrace that is ideal for nature viewing and sundowners. Every tent was made with a thatched roof for additional sun and rain protection.
A 1-night stay in a cottage at Bwana Tembo Safari Camp costs US$ 67 per person, per night. Check-in time is between 3:00 pm and 6:00 pm while checkout time is 10:00 am.
An extra bed can be provided in the rooms upon request. For children aged 4-12, it costs $50 per night per child. A cot can also be provided for children aged 0-3. This is a complimentary offer.
Dining at Bwana Tembo Safari Camp
Bwana Tembo is an Italian managed camp, this makes it possible for Italian cuisines which are mainly prepared. Standardized fresh, homemade Italian food is prepared which is more delicious.
The best pasta and wine you could taste in Uganda are found here. All the chefs are well-trained and experienced. The restaurant also serves great regional cuisine in addition to Italian specialties.
Breakfast options include continental and à la carte. Your tea, coffee or porridge can be served with snacks or fruits.
The bar serves a variety of soft, hard, and alcoholic beverages.

Getting There and Around | Murchison Falls National Park
Getting There
Search for:
Hit Enter to search or Esc key to close
The oldest and largest national park in Uganda, Murchison Falls is home to about 76 mammals and over 400 bird species, with the historical mighty falls. It is a place that will make you appreciate nature and the beauty in the wilderness. It is a perfect choice for those who love unique wildlife-viewing experiences. Murchison Falls National Park can be accessed from Kampala, the capital city of Uganda by road and is approximately 300 km from Kampala.
Quick Directions
By road, the Nile River crossing at Paraa, in the center of the park, is approximately 5hrs drive from Kampala (305km). Paraa is 85km from Masindi town by the direct route. A longer (135km) alternative route passes through Budongo forest and enjoys spectacular views across Lake Albert from the rift valley escarpment above Butiaba. Paraa can also be approached from the north via Chobe Gate near Karuma Falls, Tangi Gate near Pakwach (25km to Paraa), and Wankwar Gate near Purongo.
By Air
Murchison Falls National Park can also be reached by air. Charter flights can land at airstrips north of the Nile at Pakuba (19kms from Paraa) and south at Bugungu (13kms from Paraa).
By Road
From Kampala, you pass through Luweero and Nakasongora area with a visit to the Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary in Nakasongora. You then branch off from River Kafu and pass via Masindi, which is the nearest route. The other alternative is passing via Karuma and proceeding to Pakwach, entering through the Pakwach gate.
Apart from the road, there are also chattered flights into the park and regular flights that fly from Entebbe to Pakuba airstrip, from where you can be picked up and transferred to the booked accommodation.
By road, the Nile River crossing at Paraa, in the center of the park, is approximately 5hrs drive from Kampala (305km). Paraa is 85km from Masindi town by the direct route. A longer (135km) alternative route passes through Budongo forest and enjoys spectacular views across Lake Albert from the rift valley escarpment above Butiaba. Paraa can also be approached from the north via Chobe Gate near Karuma Falls, Tangi Gate near Pakwach (25km to Paraa), and Wankwar Gate near Purongo. Murchison can also be reached by air. Charter flights can land at airstrips north of the Nile at Pakuba (19kms from Paraa) and south at Bugungu (13kms from Paraa).
A long day s drive from Kampala, with a possible overnight break at Masindi. There is only one public means of transport from Kampala to Masindi town.
You can easily travel to Murchison Falls National Park with a rental car from one of the car rental agencies listed on this website. You can rent a car with a driver or even opt for a self-drive safari in Uganda.
Travel to Murchison Falls National Park
Murchison Falls National Park is found in northwestern Uganda. Getting there is very easy. The journey to Murchison Falls National Park takes around 5 hours on a road trip from Kampala, the capital city of Uganda about 312km.  The shortest route is from Masindi town to Paraa, it covers a distance of about 85km.

Routes
It is easy to travel to Uganda’s Murchison Falls National Park.
The Nile river crossing at Paraa, in the park’s heart, is about a 512-hour drive from Kampala by road (305km).
The direct route from Masindi to Paraa is 85 kilometers.
The rift valley escarpment above Butiaba provides stunning views across Lake Albert on a longer (135km) alternative route that passes through Budongo forest.
Chobe Gate near Karuma Falls, Tangi Gate near Pakwach (25km to Paraa), and Wankwar Gate near Purongo are all options for getting to Paraa from the north.
At Paraa, a vehicle ferry crosses the Nile.
With the exception of 13.00, this runs every hour between 07.00 and 19.00.
Murchison is also accessible by air.
Accessibility to the Park
The longer route covers about 135km from the gate. Alternatively, you may decide to take the Budongo forest route that provides you with magnificent views overlooking Lake Albert from the position of the rift valley escarpment over Butiaba.
It is possible to access Paraa from the north of the park through Chobe gate, Karuma Falls along Tangi gate.  The gate that is close to Pakwach covers an area of about 25km sq. to Paraa in addition to the Wankwar gate close to Purango.
Murchison Falls can be accessed by air. Pakuba is the landing site for chartered flights and takes about 19 km from Paraa. Bugungu covers an area of 13kms from Paraa.
The way to Murchison Falls National Park gives travelers a chance to experience the white rhinos at the Ziwa rhino sanctuary. The pearl of Africa was home to several rhinos but due to extensive poaching, the rhinos vanished.
Getting Around the Murchison Falls National Park on a Self-Driver.
The largest and oldest national park in Uganda, Murchison Falls is home to a rich variety of species, breathtaking scenery, and the powerful Nile River. Murchison Falls provides the ideal chance for an adventurous tourist looking for the independence of a self-drive safari to explore at your own speed. Come along as I show you how to get about this famous park on your own two wheels.

Uganda Accommodation & Safari Lodges | Murchison Falls National Park
Accommodation
Search for:
Hit Enter to search or Esc key to close
Murchison Falls National Park lies at the northern end of the Albertine Rift Valley, is one of the most popular national parks in Uganda and it conducts several interesting activities such as; launch trips (boat cruises), excellent game viewing, birding, visiting the top of Murchison falls, and sport fishing. There are several accommodations in the park and these range from camps to lodges.
Some of the accommodations include;
Budget Lodge
Budongo eco lodge
Red Chilli Safari Camp
Twiga Safari Lodge
Midrange Lodge
Pakuba Lodge,
Sambiya River lodge,
Kabalega Wilderness Camp,
Murchison River Lodge
Luxury safari Lodges
Paraa Safari lodge,
Chobe safari Lodge,
Bakers Lodge
Uganda Wildlife Authority campsites exist at the top of the Falls, Rabongo forest and Delta Point. These sites provide pit latrines and in some cases, basic showers. Budget accommodation and camping is available at Red Chilli Rest Camp and Kaniyo Pabidi Camp. More upmarket accommodation is provided by Nile Safari Camp, Sambiya River and Paraa Safari Lodges. In Masindi, the Masindi Hotel and Court View Hotel are recommended.
There are upmarket lodges and a luxury tented camps. There are lots of places to stay in while on a safari in the Murchison Falls National Park,
Visitors to this Park will live comfortably in its fantastic accommodations:
Chobe Safari Lodge, Luxury
This 5-stars’ lodge offers breathtaking panoramic views, coupled with the sounds of the River Nile s magnificent rapids, sets the scene for a Uganda safari adventure that will impress even the most discerning of visitors. The lodge provides a great opportunity to sample the wildlife, birds, flora and fauna; all in an area of the park that has yet to be discovered. This area of the Park is suitable for fishing, and will revive this newly refurbished lodge to become one of the best fishing destinations in Africa.
Chobe lodge boasts 36 elegant guestrooms, 21 luxury tents, 4 suites and a Presidential Cottage. The River Nile is the main focus from an architect’s perspective, and so all the rooms and luxury tents have balconies and terraces facing the magnificent sweeping views. The facilities at the lodge include; a unique swimming pool, Karuma restaurant & cuisine, gift shop, business centre, Karuma bar & terrace, conference facilities, and Chobe health club & spa. The lodge organizes various amazing activities, such as; sport fishing, bush breakfast, visiting the top of Murchison falls, nature walks, and safari drives.
Paraa Safari Lodge, Luxury
Paraa Safari Lodge is one of the best and highly recommended accommodations in Murchison Falls National Park. The lodge overlooks one of nature s best kept secrets, the River Nile, on its journey from its source at Lake Victoria to join Lake Albert – here it is suddenly channeled into a gorge only six meters wide, and cataracts 43 meters below. Paraa Safari Lodge offers a unique blend of comfort, relaxation and adventure, and each of the rooms at Paraa is a haven of style and serenity, complete with balcony and private bathroom.
There are 54 rooms at Paraa Safari Lodge complete with balcony and en-suite private bathroom. The choice of accommodation at the lodge varies – a cottage, suites, double, twin and single. The lodge’s facilities include; an elegant outdoor pool, restaurant & cuisine, a business centre, gift shop, conference facilities, the explorer’s bar. Among the activities offered at the lodge, include; chimpanzee tracking, birding, safari drives, visiting the top of Uganda’s greatest waterfall (Murchison falls), boat trips to delta, bush breakfast, nature walks, and fishing.
Baker’s Lodge, Luxury
Baker’s Lodge is sits on the southern shores of the mighty Nile River which transects Murchison Falls National Park. The lodge derived its name from an English explorer Sir Samuel White Baker. This intimate, safari styled lodge is set within a large private area with direct river access, large shady trees and wetland areas hosting abundant birdlife along the water’s edge. The views onto the river are vast and just extraordinary with islands hosting nesting egret birds, elephants bathing and pods of hippos regularly viewed.
Baker’s lodge comprises of ten suites and each of them is raised from the ground on supporting pillars with its own deck overlooking the river.  Much care has been taken to ensure each of the ten suites has privacy as well as superb views either up or down stream.  The large, airy facilities are fan cooled, have netted windows with opening options, customized solid wooden furniture, and hanging mosquito nets and especially selected locally crafted items for the accessories. The en-suite bathrooms are open plan with solar hot water showers and baths with a view in some units. Solar lighting completes the services for this eco-friendly top quality establishment.
Enjoy the various fantastic activities in Murchison Falls National Park while basing in the amazing Baker’s Lodge. Among the activities to enjoy in the Park include; visiting the top of the falls, game drives and game viewing, birding, fishing, boat cruises, nature walks, hot air balloon safaris, and chimpanzee tracking.
Nile Safari Lodge
This luxurious eco-lodge is ideally located on the southern shores of River Nile amid the well-to-do papyrus forest. The lodge is designed to with beautiful wooden chalets along with lavishness tents that are located in a perfect area to conduct spectacular views of the park along with the African wilderness. The most exciting aspect about this lodge is that natural feel that you experience when you get close to the environment.
